description: Read royal faces, visit a troublesome king and climb the battlefield before following Charles II to his escape pub.
short_description: Track three kings through the final battle of the English Civil War.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
recommended_age: Recommended 14+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A city-centre loop with a steep climb to a surfaced hilltop park and ordinary road crossings.

before_you_go.terrain: A city-centre loop with a steep climb to a hilltop park and normal road crossings. Use the park’s surfaced public paths.
before_you_go.hills: Includes a notable steep section; take your time and use a suitable alternative where available.
before_you_go.steps: No required steps are known, though temporary diversions may vary.
before_you_go.accessibility: Steep gradients and historic surfaces may be difficult; check a step-free alternative before setting off.
before_you_go.toilets: Check local public facilities before setting off; customer toilets may depend on opening hours.
before_you_go.footwear: Supportive, grippy walking shoes are recommended.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the finishing venue’s current dog policy before entering.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Possible but the steep section and historic surfaces may be demanding.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin beneath two stone Charleses and a queen who watches justice from above.
stops.Hint_1: Find the grand Queen Anne building on the High Street.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the statues of Charles I, Charles II and Queen Anne on the Guildhall façade.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Worcester Guildhall was begun in 1721, probably to designs by local stonemason Thomas White. It combined city government with civil and assize courts, and even contained prison cells.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find the final bed of the king forced to seal Magna Carta, guarded by a prince who never became king.
stops.Hint_1: Walk south along the High Street to the cathedral.
stops.Hint_2: King John and Prince Arthur Tudor are both buried inside.
stops.Unlock_Fact: King John, who sealed Magna Carta in 1215, was buried at Worcester Cathedral after his death in 1216. The cathedral also contains the ornate chantry of Prince Arthur, Henry VIII's elder brother.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Climb where royal guns turned against their owners in the last great battle of the Civil Wars.
stops.Hint_1: Head east past Sidbury and climb into Fort Royal Park.
stops.Hint_2: Find the hilltop park behind The Commandery.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Fort Royal was a Royalist earthwork in the Battle of Worcester on 3 September 1651, the final major battle of the English Civil War. Parliamentary troops captured it and turned its guns on the retreating Royalists.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Finish where a defeated king slipped away from Worcester and began six weeks on the run.
stops.Hint_2: Find the timber-framed King Charles House at number 29.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! King Charles II is believed to have escaped through this 1577 building after defeat at Worcester in 1651. It is now a pub and restaurant serving local ales and food if open.
